app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

symptoms.potential_symptom: Service experiencing sustained high request latency, with traces up to ~10.8s and evidence of repeated proxy hops
symptoms.evidence: 30 slow traces observed (traces_count=30). Max latency 10834.846 ms (trace 9e35c0288a7e5a8a716e4885396464bd). Many traces show sequences with repeated proxy hops involving frontend-proxy (e.g., 'frontend-proxy -> frontend -> frontend-proxy -> frontend -> ad', 'frontend-proxy -> frontend -> frontend-proxy -> frontend -> frontend-proxy -> frontend -> ad'), and one trace shows frontend-proxy alone with 3151.422 ms latency (trace 2f65cff122c5b824d7e82fd0c9a87f11). No error spans or metric anomalies reported.

symptoms.potential_symptom: Service handling amplified request work (multiple frontend spans per request) causing elevated end-to-end latency
symptoms.evidence: Multiple slow traces include repeated invocations of frontend within a single trace (examples: trace 3e2b729f0034530a2802cafcd26b9f55 latency 10789.93 ms sequence 'frontend-proxy -> frontend -> frontend-proxy -> frontend -> frontend-proxy -> frontend -> ad'; trace ab3d4731417221797857dcddcc0c5dd3 latency 7614.096 ms similar loop). These patterns indicate frontend is called multiple times per request and is present in the high-latency call paths. No error spans or anomalous pod/metric status reported.

rca_tasks.investigation_goal: Epicenter check (platform/latency): Confirm whether repeated proxy hops/loops originate at frontend-proxy by inspecting slow traces and a representative full trace to see the exact span sequence, timing breakdown, and where time is spent. Hypothesis: Envoy/frontend-proxy routing is causing request amplification/loops (proxy->frontend->proxy) rather than backend processing. Use traces to prove loop origin. Data dependencies: frontend pod(s) [frontend-559ccb996b-zrl4g]; also chatbot/image-provider referenced but not primary.

Connection check (config/route mismatch) between frontend-proxy and frontend — two-sided verification of routing: (A) inspect frontend-proxy routing/envoy config or Deployment/ConfigMap for the upstream/cluster entry used for 'frontend' (hostname, port, path, virtual host) and (B) inspect Kubernetes Service/Endpoints for 'frontend' to verify matching port/name/endpoints. Hypothesis: frontend-proxy route points to the wrong host/port or to itself causing re-entry loops. Data dependencies: frontend pod(s) [frontend-559ccb996b-zrl4g].

Connection check (two-sided) between frontend and ad — verify frontend's config/clients for 'ad' (URL/port/grpc target) and inspect 'ad' Kubernetes Service and endpoints for matching port/name and healthy endpoints. Hypothesis: misconfigured target/port for 'ad' causes retries/slow calls that amplify latency. Data dependencies: ad pod(s) [ad-c759f8b78-2k74g].

Connection check (two-sided) between frontend and product-catalog — inspect frontend callsite/config for product-catalog (host/port/timeout/retries) and inspect 'product-catalog' Service/Endpoints for port/name and pod readiness. Hypothesis: product-catalog endpoint mismatch or incorrect port/headers triggers slow calls or retries that inflate frontend latency. Data dependencies: product-catalog pod(s) [product-catalog-b74dfc8b6-67q2f].

Connection check (two-sided) between frontend and recommendation — inspect frontend config/code for recommendation target (URL/GRPC metadata/timeouts) and inspect 'recommendation' Service/Endpoints for port/name and healthy pods. Hypothesis: backend misaddressing or incompatible protocol causes extra hops/latency. Data dependencies: recommendation pod(s) [recommendation-b6976ff4c-7t2qj].

Connection check (two-sided) between frontend and cart — inspect frontend's cart client config (Valkey/cart URL, port, timeouts) and inspect 'cart' Service/Endpoints for matching port/name and pod readiness. Hypothesis: cart calls (synchronous or via valkey) are misdirected or slow and contributing to amplified frontend spans. Data dependencies: cart pod(s) [cart-5df68c7b56-gnggf].

Connection check (two-sided) between frontend and checkout — inspect frontend's checkout client config (URL/port/timeouts/retries) and inspect 'checkout' Service/Endpoints for port/name and healthy pods. Hypothesis: checkout calls are misconfigured causing cascading synchronous waits that amplify request time. Data dependencies: checkout pod(s) [checkout-6598d86d4b-s89nr].

Connection check (two-sided) between frontend and shipping — inspect frontend's shipping client config (URL/port/timeouts) and inspect 'shipping' Service/Endpoints for matching port/name and pod readiness. Hypothesis: shipping remote calls are slow/misaddressed and contributing to end-to-end amplification. Data dependencies: shipping pod(s) [shipping-68f877fd46-t6gc9].

Connection check (two-sided) between frontend and currency — inspect frontend's currency conversion client (endpoint/port/timeout) and inspect 'currency' Service/Endpoints for port/name and healthy endpoints. Hypothesis: slow currency calls or misconfigured target cause amplified frontend latency. Data dependencies: currency pod(s) [currency-64f59cbc98-dpqx5].

Service-level check (app/latency) for frontend: confirm whether frontend itself is amplifying work per incoming request (multiple outbound calls or re-entrancy) by checking frontend logs and traces correlated to the slow traces to find repeated incoming HTTP/gRPC entries or retry logic. Hypothesis: frontend code or middleware is re-invoking itself (or not detecting proxied requests) causing multiple internal calls per external request. Data dependencies: frontend pod(s) [frontend-559ccb996b-zrl4g].

rca_analyses_list.diagnosis: Routing loop/amplification caused by frontend service calling the frontend-proxy address: requests are being routed frontend-proxy -> frontend -> frontend-proxy -> frontend (multiple times), causing high latency.
rca_analyses_list.reasoning: Trace 6f873117ddfc5a9c9ed1a40a96bd7cc1 shows repeated Envoy client egress spans (operationName 'router frontend egress', e.g. spanIDs 3459d2ebf62fb225, 6461811e16173e24, cdc0e0c8fbe84542, 63ecf7aca6047d2d, 84ba03f264af288c, cd75b39bc66d7a6e) with upstream_cluster='frontend' and long durations (e.g. cd75b39bc66d7a6e duration ~50,376 ms). Matching server spans (e.g. e918d771ce0af83d, a23f02d0c27ec94e, a6151c8b97d65e04, 17285535b205be00) show server.address='frontend-proxy' and http.url values like 'http://frontend-proxy:8080/api/cart' and '/api/checkout', proving the frontend service is issuing HTTP calls to the frontend-proxy hostname. The top-level trace sequence (and the trace list) explicitly contains repeated alternations of 'frontend-proxy' and 'frontend' (and cart), confirming the proxy->frontend->proxy amplification loop originates at frontend-proxy being called by frontend. These spans and URLs directly identify the misrouting loop as the root cause of the elevated latency.

task.investigation_goal: Epicenter check (platform/latency): Confirm whether repeated proxy hops/loops originate at frontend-proxy by inspecting slow traces and a representative full trace to see the exact span sequence, timing breakdown, and where time is spent. Hypothesis: Envoy/frontend-proxy routing is causing request amplification/loops (proxy->frontend->proxy) rather than backend processing. Use traces to prove loop origin. Data dependencies: frontend pod(s) [frontend-559ccb996b-zrl4g]; also chatbot/image-provider referenced but not primary.

insights: Multiple traces showed elevated latency with repeated alternation of 'frontend-proxy' and 'frontend' in the trace sequence; one trace (6f873117...) exhibited extreme amplification (many proxy/frontend hops) and total observed latency spikes (~103.6 ms in the list, and individual proxy egress spans up to ~50,376 ms in the full trace).

Envoy/router client egress spans consistently reported upstream_cluster='frontend' and long durations (several egress spans had multi-second to 50s durations), indicating repeated proxy->frontend remote calls rather than network errors or timeouts.

Server spans handling requests show server.address='frontend-proxy' and http.url values referencing 'http://frontend-proxy:8080/...', proving the frontend service is issuing HTTP requests to the frontend-proxy hostname. This creates frontend->frontend-proxy calls in addition to the proxy->frontend routing, producing a loop/amplification.

All HTTP/gRPC spans returned success status codes (200 / grpc OK) — behavior is functionally successful but misrouted. The problem is a logical routing/misconfiguration loop (calls to proxy hostname from the frontend), not a downstream service crash or error-returning failure.

Dependencies implicated: frontend-proxy (Envoy) routes requests to frontend (upstream_cluster=frontend); frontend is calling the frontend-proxy host, which causes the proxy to re-route back to frontend repeatedly. Cart and other services appear as typical downstream services invoked by frontend during the loop, contributing spans but not producing error responses.

Confirmed hypothesis: root cause is misrouting caused by the frontend service calling the frontend-proxy address (hostname), creating a request amplification/routing loop between frontend and frontend-proxy and causing the observed high latency.

Impact summary: increased request latency and amplified tracing spans (repeated proxy/client hops) leading to degraded performance; services still returned success codes so functional correctness remained but performance was impacted.
Action taken: final diagnosis submitted identifying the routing loop/amplification (frontend calling frontend-proxy) as the root cause.

rca_analyses_list.reasoning: 1) frontend-proxy Deployment environment shows FRONTEND_HOST=frontend and FRONTEND_PORT=8080 (env vars used by the proxy image to configure Envoy upstream). 2) frontend Service exposes port 8080 -> targetPort 8080 and its Endpoints are 10.244.1.34:8080. 3) The frontend pod (frontend-559ccb996b-zrl4g) has IP 10.244.1.34 and container port 8080. These two unique findings confirm the proxy is pointing at the correct service/port and the Service resolves to the actual frontend pod (not the proxy), so the suspected host/port or self-loop misroute is not present.

insights: frontend-proxy Deployment is configured to forward to frontend:8080 (env vars FRONTEND_HOST=frontend, FRONTEND_PORT=8080, ENVOY_PORT=8080).
The 'frontend' Service is a ClusterIP (10.96.89.212) exposing port 8080 -> targetPort 8080 and has Endpoint 10.244.1.34:8080.
The frontend pod (frontend-559ccb996b-zrl4g) has IP 10.244.1.34, exposes container port 8080, is Running and Ready, and is the Service endpoint.
No self-loop or misrouting detected: the Service endpoints point to the frontend pod IP, not the frontend-proxy pod, so the proxy is not resolving to itself.
Both Deployment and Service appear healthy (frontend-proxy has 1/1 replica available; frontend pod is Ready).
The hypothesis that the frontend-proxy Envoy/bootstrap or Service configuration pointed to the wrong host/port (causing a loop or misroute) is disproven.
Final conclusion: there is no routing/config mismatch between frontend-proxy and frontend; this is not the root cause of the incident.

final_report.root_cause: The frontend service is misconfigured to issue HTTP requests to the frontend-proxy hostname (requests use URLs like http://frontend-proxy:8080/...), which creates a routing amplification/loop: frontend-proxy -> frontend -> frontend-proxy -> frontend ... . This loop causes repeated proxy egress and server ingress hops, dramatically increasing end-to-end latency. A secondary contributor was an unstable ad pod (ad-c759f8b78-2k74g) that experienced OOMKills (Exit Code 137) and restarts, causing intermittent unavailability and additional retries/latency, but this did not create the proxy loop.
final_report.evidence_summary: Priority #1 traces: multiple high-latency traces (up to ~10.8s) show repeated alternation of 'frontend-proxy' and 'frontend' spans. Full trace analysis shows Envoy/router egress spans with upstream_cluster='frontend' and matching server spans whose server.address='frontend-proxy' and http.url values like 'http://frontend-proxy:8080/api/cart' and '/api/checkout' — proving the frontend service is issuing requests to the proxy hostname and causing the proxy->frontend->proxy loop. Priority #2: frontend-proxy Envoy upstream and Kubernetes Service for frontend are correctly configured (frontend-proxy points to the frontend Service; Service endpoints point to the frontend pod), so the loop is not caused by proxy misconfiguration. Priority #3: frontend targets ad:8080 correctly, but the ad pod (ad-c759f8b78-2k74g) shows Last State Exit Code 137 and RestartCount=2 with BackOff events, indicating OOM/kills and intermittent unavailability that contributed to retries and additional latency.
final_report.investigation_summary: Investigations prioritized by likelihood: (1) Epicenter check of traces (completed) confirmed repeated proxy/frontend hops and identified HTTP calls from frontend to 'frontend-proxy' in span tags/URLs — direct proof of frontend-originated routing loops. (2) Two-sided config check between frontend-proxy and frontend (completed) showed correct Envoy/upstream and Service/Endpoints mappings, ruling out proxy pointing at itself. (3) Two-sided check between frontend and ad (completed) found ad pod instability (OOMKills) causing intermittent latency contributions. Multiple kubectl_describe and trace retrievals were performed and correlated with span tag data to build the causal chain. No error-status responses were observed in spans (200/grpc OK), supporting that this was a logical/misrouting performance issue rather than functional failures. Given the direct trace evidence and supporting Kubernetes config/pod state data, the investigation is complete and the root cause is localized.
